data.name: Ingram
data.description:
A talking crow who repeatedly appears to speak to Ryo and warn him against going into the forest. He is actually the son of Venna, Ingram, turned into a crow for disobeying her.

• Big Damn Heroes: In the true ending, when Venna is about to kill Ryo, Ingram shows up and holds her off so he can escape. • Brutal Honesty: He has no issue with speaking his mind around Ryo. • The Cameo: Appears in a picture at Rune's room in Blackout Hospital. He still has his Glasgow Grin, implying that the events of Crowscare happened in that timeline as well. • Cassandra Truth: Keeps trying to warn Ryo about how dangerous Venna is, but it always goes on deaf ears. • Forced Transformation: He was originally of the same species as Venna, but was turned into a crow as punishment for disobedience. • Glasgow Grin: A non-villainous example. In the true ending, Venna carves a bloody smile into him while trying to kill him in the finale. He does get it stitched up later, though. • Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He is very blunt and often harsh to Ryo when telling him to stay away from the woods and Venna, but only because he genuinely wants to protect Ryo from an evil, manipulative witch. • Little Bit Beastly: Like his mother (Venna), he is a humanoid crow. Though he spends most of the game in bird form thanks to being cursed by his mother for disobedience.

• Matricide: In the true end, he kills his abusive mother Venna in defense of Ryo. • Talking Animal: A talking crow. According to Ryo, he's far from the first he's met. Ryo: BOO! Crow: You don't scare me, kid. Ryo: Whoaaaa—you can talk! Crow: Yeah... what about it? Ryo: Oh, no, nothing! I've met plenty of talking birds before! I just... • Two Aliases, One Character: The talking crow, Venna's son, and Ingram are all the same individual. • Walking Spoiler: Saying too much about him will give away his true identity. • Would Hit a Girl: "Hit" is an understatement; he kills Venna (his Abusive Mom) off-screen in the true ending. While done in defense of Ryo, it is depicted as creepy.
